newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tele Danmark says new rules cost less than thought.
newsitem.headline: Tele Danmark says new rules cost less than thought.

text.p: Danish telecoms group Tele Danmark said on Friday that it expected new Danish telecommunications regulations to cut its full-year 1997 pre-tax profits by between 0.4 and 0.9 billion crowns.
It had earlier predicted that the legislation would cost the company between 0.5 and 1.0 billion crowns.
Danish deregulation laws cap the prices that Tele Danmark can charge for giving competitors access to its fixed-line network and impose a range of technical conditions.
A Tele Danmark statement said that its 1996 pre-tax profit was 5.1 billion crowns.
The company's share price slipped by one crown after the announcement, to 320.00 crowns. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
